findings.quote: Red dwarfs, the smallest stars, burn fuel so slowly that they live far longer than the present age of the universe.
findings.problem: Not raised in round 1; it moved word for word from the parent. 'The smallest stars' is a general statement that fails against stars the lesson itself names. Red dwarfs are the smallest main-sequence stars, but the lesson calls a white dwarf 'a small, hot, faint star about as wide as Earth' and gives a neutron star as 'about $20$ km across'. Even the smallest red dwarfs are several times wider than Earth. The lesson's Size section uses 'small' for width, so a student reading this sentence learns that red dwarfs are smaller than white dwarfs and neutron stars, and would answer a 'smallest kind of star' question wrongly. The statement holds only with the limit 'main-sequence' (or 'lowest-mass').
findings.source: Checklist B01; reader-rules.md 'Added after the Sol audit'; NASA Science, Star Types, https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stars/types/ (red dwarfs are 'the smallest main sequence stars'; a white dwarf is 'usually Earth-size'; a neutron star is about as wide as Manhattan is long)
